Synopsis:
    Oscar-winning director Laura Poitras and co-director Rachel Lauren Mueller premiered a 25-minute documentary at the Venice Film Festival chronicling ICE deportation raids in Minneapolis and the community resistance they triggered. The film documents volunteer tracking networks, confrontations with agents, and the story of a Mexican man hiding from authorities. Filmmakers argue the operation's eventual partial rollback — ICE reducing agents by 80% — validates grassroots resistance. The piece is primarily a cultural/political commentary on Trump's immigration enforcement campaign.
